transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Partnerships), Maria Gomez (NexusCloud Partnerships), Rajiv Patel (Nexus Cloud Sales), Ellen Li (Nexus PM), Omar Haddad (Infra)

Summary: quick partner intro between Redwood and NexusCloud to explore cloud/GPU integration, go-to-market motions, and technical feasibility for a co-sell + managed infra offering. Discussed Nexus's GPU fleet, networking/VPC constraints, security/compliance ask, and next steps for benchmarks and partner agreement.

Topics: partner GTM, technical integration (VPC peering, private control plane), supported GPUs and instance types, pricing/sizing, security (SOC2/KMS), pilot scope and timeline.

[00:00] Sofia Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time, I'm Sofia from Redwood, AE on the partnerships front, with Liam who's our solutions engineer. Quick round robin?
[00:18] Maria Gomez: Hi — Maria here from Nexus, head of partnerships. Rajiv and Ellen are on as well.
[00:25] Rajiv Patel: Hi all.
[00:27] Liam Chen: Hey — Liam from Redwood SE.
[00:30] Ellen Li: Ellen, technical PM.
[00:33] Omar Haddad: Omar — infra engineer.
[00:35] Sofia Patel: Great. Agenda — quick intros, high level on Nexus infra and go-to-market, then Liam will go through Redwood's runtime and typical integration patterns, and we'll finish with next steps. Anything to add?
[00:45] Maria Gomez: No that's fine.

[01:02] Rajiv Patel: To give context — NexusCloud runs a multi-tenant cloud, we have a mix of A100 and upcoming H100 fleets in a couple of regions. We're looking to establish partnerships with inference platforms to offer managed LLM inference as a value-add, and also potentially co-selling managed nodes to our enterprise customers. Key constraints are tenancy isolation, private networking (VPC peering or private link), and compliance for financial customers.
[01:30] Sofia Patel: Makes sense — similar asks we see with other cloud partners. Can you share current scale — GPU count, typical sequence lengths or workloads?
[01:40] Ellen Li: Roughly 400 GPUs today in prod, mostly A100s, planning to add H100 in Q1. Workloads are a mix — LLM generative chat for customers (seq len ~512 typical), embeddings batch jobs overnight, and some large batch inferencing for vector search re-ranks.
[02:05] Omar Haddad: Note — network egress is heavily metered, so anything requiring heavy traffic back to Redwood hosted control plane is a blocker unless we do private deployment.

[02:20] Liam Chen: Totally understood. Quick overview of Redwood: we offer hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private deployment — the private deployment can run in your VPC with a private control plane so audit logs, KMS integration, and traffic stays inside. Our runtime supports A100/H100 and we do kernel selection, quantization-friendly paths, and KV cache to reduce token cost.
[02:50] Maria Gomez: Can you run inside a customer's VPC? We need the control plane to live in our network for some customers.
[02:58] Liam Chen: Yes, we have a private option — customer-managed control plane deployed into your VPC or on-prem. We integrate with KMS/HSM for key management, and can wire up SSO/SAML and RBAC to your enterprise directory.
[03:15] Rajiv Patel: How do you handle model variants and fallbacks? We want predictable SLAs and graceful degradation when capacity is limited.
[03:25] Liam Chen: We have smart routing with policy-based fallbacks — for example route to cheaper quantized model variants or alternate region/pool. For Dedicated/reserved pools we guarantee throughput with autoscaling policies. Fallbacks are configurable.

[04:00] Ellen Li: On the private deployment: what are the networking requirements — do you need egress, special ports, or just internal communications?
[04:10] Liam Chen: For private control plane in your VPC, we mainly need internal endpoints, access to your KMS endpoint if using customer-managed keys, and optional metrics ingestion into your Prometheus. No mandatory egress back to Redwood unless you want our hosted observability.

[04:40] Omar Haddad: Ok but we might want to keep logs in-house for some banks — can we route audit logs to our SIEM?
[04:47] Priya Nair: Yes we support audit log export and can push to S3 or a syslog endpoint; many partners hook it up to their SIEM — we should capture that as a requirement.

[05:05] Maria Gomez: From GTM side — Nexus wants marketing co-sell, joint collateral, and a referral pricing/ rev share model. What are typical partner models you offer?
[05:20] Sofia Patel: We do a few things — referral fee for customer introductions, co-sell discounts on committed Dedicated capacity, and joint solutions pricing for white-label private deployments. We can share standard partner tiers and revenue share ranges — we'll follow up with a draft.

[06:00] Rajiv Patel: Pricing is crucial — our sales team needs an example of cost per qps and per-token economics so we can model margins.
[06:12] Liam Chen: We'll prepare a baseline — token cost breakdown, GPU cost normalization, and how batching/kv caching changes unit economics. For benchmarks, we recommend a small pilot workload on a reserved test cluster to measure latency and cost for your sequences.

[06:40] Ellen Li: Onbenchmarks — can Redwood run a test harness and provide a latency/cost baseline for H100 vs A100? We are evaluating which GPU to promote to customers.
[06:50] Liam Chen: Yes, we can run microbenchmarks and a larger workload test. We'll need sample prompts and typical concurrency. Also need access details to provision a test environment (or we can provision a Redwood-managed test cluster in a Nexus VPC).

[07:20] Omar Haddad: Security questions — SOC2, ISO certs, pen test reports. Also data residency for EU customers — can keys and data stay in region?
[07:32] Priya Nair: Redwood is SOC2-compliant and we can provide attestation; region-based deployments for data residency are supported with private deployment. KMS can be customer-managed in-region. We'll send the security pack.

[08:05] Maria Gomez: Any limitations on model licensing? Some of our enterprise customers require specific model licensing terms and auditability.
[08:15] Liam Chen: We have a model catalog with open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles. Licensing varies by model; for enterprise we accommodate bring-your-own-model or pin to vetted variants. License terms would be part of the partner/pilot agreement.

[09:00] Rajiv Patel: On integration: how mature are your connectors for billing and marketplace? We need seamless billing to our customers via our metering APIs.
[09:12] Sofia Patel: We have APIs and webhooks for usage and metering; many partners integrate via an aggregator or a direct billing API. We can map usage events to your billing system — we'll need Nexus's metering API swagger and a product team integration contact.

[10:00] Maria Gomez: Great. Any reference partners doing similar integrations?
[10:08] Priya Nair: We've worked with Velascale and Aurora GPU partners on similar flows; can provide a contact and case study.

[10:30] Ellen Li: Quick technical clarifying question — for KV cache and prefix caching, what's the memory footprint per request? Concerned about memory on multi-tenant hosts.
[10:40] Liam Chen: It depends on seq length and model size. Our runtime manages KV cache and we can configure per-tenant cache limits; for multi-tenant you'll likely want isolated pools or qos limits to avoid noisy neighbor issues. We'll include memory footprint estimates in the benchmark doc.

[12:00] Sofia Patel: For the pilot scope, propose: 1) benchmark run on a small reserved H100 pool in Nexus VPC, 2) run customer workload sample (chat + embeddings) for two weeks, 3) joint evaluation and GTM planning session. Thoughts?
[12:18] Rajiv Patel: Sounds good — timeline wise we'd aim to start pilot in early Dec. We have procurement cycles but partnerships team can move faster.
[12:30] Maria Gomez: We'll aim for a decision by mid-Dec if benchmarks look good.

[13:00] Omar Haddad: On provisioning — what's required from our infra team to stand up the private control plane?
[13:10] Liam Chen: We'll provide IaC templates (Terraform) to deploy the control plane into your VPC, required subnets, security group rules, and KMS endpoints. For metrics and logs we can wire to your endpoints.

[14:00] Ellen Li: Any concerns about software compatibility with our orchestration? We use Nomad + Kubernetes hybrid for scheduling.
[14:10] Liam Chen: We support Kubernetes, and our deployment templates can be adapted; our SEs will work with your infra team on compatibility tests. Nomad customers we've worked with used a Kubernetes overlay for the Redwood components.

[15:00] Maria Gomez: Let's capture immediate asks — security pack, partner deck, example pricing, and a benchmark plan.
[15:10] Sofia Patel: Agreed. Action items noted.

[15:30] Rajiv Patel: On commercial model — we prefer a co-sell discount for committed capacity plus a referral fee on self-serve customers. Can we get a sample term sheet?
[15:42] Sofia Patel: Yes, Priya will draft the referral and rev share ranges and we'll attach sample commercial terms.

[16:00] (brief cross-talk about calendar times)

[20:00] (technical deep-dive scheduling discussion)

[34:00] Liam Chen: To reiterate technical next steps: provide sample prompts, concurrency targets, and a small dataset for embeddings to run in the benchmark. We'll set up a 2-week test window.

[40:00] Maria Gomez: We'll prepare the dataset and procurement folks will review the pilot SOW.

[48:00] Sofia Patel: Alright thanks everyone — recap: Redwood to send partner deck, security pack, and sizing + pricing example; Nexus to share fleet profile, test prompts, and procurement contacts; schedule technical deep-dive w/ infra next week.

[48:30] Maria Gomez: Thanks all. Looking forward to it.

[48:35] Rajiv Patel: Thanks.

[48:40] Liam Chen: Thanks — we'll follow up via email with links and the next meeting invite.

[48:45] Sofia Patel: Meeting end.

References and links mentioned: partner deck (link - to be shared), security pack (link - to be shared), benchmark spreadsheet (link - to be shared).

End of transcript.
